caseno: Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 718 of 2008
lawyer:
Abu Bakkar Siddique, Advocate (appeared with leave of the Court) instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate- on-Record ------- For the Petitioners. 
Not represented ------- The Respondents.
parties:
Janab Ali (Md) and others ------- Petitioners
Vs. 
Salema Khatun and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 4. The trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocate of the contesting parties mid having regard to the statements made in the pleadings of the respective parties found all the issues in favour of the pre-emptor and accordingly, allowed the pre-emption. The pre-emptee, being aggrieved, preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 58 of 2001 in the Court of District Judge, Mymensingh, and, on transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh, who on consideration of the materials and evidence on record allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and order passed by the trial Court and thereby rejected the pre-emption holding that the Miscellaneous Case was bad for defect of parties and the pre-emptor failed to prove the claim of co-sharership in the case jote, observing that the pre-emptor could not produce any deed in support of his claim of co-sharership by purchase in the case jote and that the persons named in the case khatian being RoR Khatian No. 50 namely, Suruj Ali, Ahained Ali and Samed Ali, were not made parties in the miscellaneous case. The pre-emptor being aggrieved, moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4578 of 2002, wherein Rule was issued and the said Rule was made absolute on contest setting aside the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court below. The High Court Division found that the suit was not bad for defect of parties and the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by purchase in the case jote observing that on the objection raised by the pre-emptee as to defect of parties the pre-emptor filed an application with interrogatories to require the pre-emptee to name the persons not made parties in the miscellaneous case but the learned Court did not pass any order in the said application and accordingly, the pre-emptor filed application for addition of parties naming the persons who were left out to the best of his knowledge and a copy of the application was served upon the pre-emptee and the pre-emptee did not raise any objection against said application for addition of party and also did not bring to the notice of the Court that apart from the persons sought to be added in the case, there were other persons needed to be added as party in the case to cure the miscellaneous case from being bad for defect of party. The pre-emptor's application for adding party was duly allowed and the pre-emptor took required steps accordingly and thereby the pre-emptee is barred from raising any objection as to defect of party on the principle of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel and that the land under pre-emption as well as land earlier purchased by the pre-emptor were of the same RoR KhatianNo. 50 (Exhibit-3) and both the purchase deed of the pre-emptor as well as the purchase deed of the pre-emptee relates to Settlement Plot No.103; the land in the deed of purchase of the pre-emptor has been described as "Hal Plot No. 577 and the land under pre-emption is described as mentioned Hal Plot No. 583 but both the aforesaid Hal Plot Nos. 577 and 583 correspond to the Settlement Plot No. 103 and thereby the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the case jote and on discussion at length the single Bench of the High Court Division has found the pre-emptor as co-sharer in the case jote and that the miscellaneous case was not bad for defect of party and the pre-emptee is barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence from raising any objection as to defect of parties.
